concepts.label: node
concepts.gloss: A node is a forwarding or switching domain within a topology that hosts termination, access, connection, adaptation, and switching-rule resources.
concepts.example: R1 is a node in the OTN-over-optical topology, hosting resources such as nep-R1-R2 and the OTU4/ODU2 adaptation.

concepts.label: link-termination-point
concepts.gloss: A link-termination-point is a node-owned edge point at which a topology link terminates, representing that link's attachment to the node.
concepts.example: nep-R1-R2 is the termination point on R1 for link-R1-R2.

concepts.label: transitional-link
concepts.gloss: A transitional link is an intra-node adaptation construct that relates layer-protocol qualifications when traffic is mapped between different transport layers.
concepts.example: At R1, the OTU4/ODU2 transitional link represents the adaptation that maps an ODU2 signal into OTU4.

concepts.label: service-interface-point
concepts.gloss: A service-interface-point is a node-associated access point through which a client requests or reaches a connectivity service.
concepts.example: sip-A1-odu is the ODU service access point on A1 used as one endpoint of cs-a1a3-odu2.

concepts.label: connectivity-service
concepts.gloss: A connectivity service is a requested end-to-end transport service over a topology, accessed through service-interface-points and realized by connection-end-points within the network.
concepts.example: cs-a1a3-odu2 provides ODU2 connectivity from A1 to A3 over the OTN-over-optical topology, using the A1 and A3 SIPs and CEPs such as cep-a1a3-R1 and cep-a1a3-R3.

concepts.label: layer-protocol-qualifier
concepts.gloss: A layer-protocol-qualifier specifies the multiplexing or adaptation context in which a connectivity service's client-layer signal is carried by a server-layer protocol.
concepts.example: For the A1-to-A3 ODU2 service, the qualifier "ODU2 mapped into OTU4" states that the ODU2 client signal is transported within OTU4.

concepts.label: node-rule-group
concepts.gloss: A node-rule-group is a node-local set of constraints or capabilities governing which terminations may be switched or cross-connected within that node.
concepts.example: The R2 cross-connect rule group determines the permitted internal cross-connections through node R2.

concepts.label: link
concepts.gloss: A link is a topology-level connectivity resource between nodes whose ends are represented by link-termination-points on those nodes.
concepts.example: link-R1-R2 connects nodes R1 and R2 and terminates at their corresponding node edge points, including nep-R1-R2 on R1.

concepts.label: topology
concepts.gloss: A topology is the scoped, potentially multi-layer network graph that contains nodes and the links between them and over which connectivity services are provided.
concepts.example: The OTN-over-optical domain is a multi-layer topology containing nodes such as R1, R2, and A1 and links such as link-R1-R2 and link-A1-R1.

concepts.label: connection-end-point
concepts.gloss: A connection-end-point is a node-local endpoint of the network connection that realizes a particular connectivity service.
concepts.example: cep-a1a3-R1 is the R1 connection endpoint belonging to the realization of the A1-to-A3 ODU2 service cs-a1a3-odu2.
